New services must use **Gateway API** (`setting: gateway-api`). The deciding file is [`policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml) in `dshnayder-org/infra`, branch `git-access-ab/r200`.

## The authoritative policy

`policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml`, verbatim:

```
# policy: ingress-class
# version: v3   effective: 2026-04-19   status: current
# subject: which ingress implementation new services must use
apiVersion: policy.meridian.io/v1
kind: FleetPolicy
metadata:
  name: ingress-class-v3
spec:
  effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19
  status: current
  setting: gateway-api
```

## Why the other two versions do not apply

The repo carries three versions of the same `ingress-class` policy. This is version history, not a conflict — each older file declares itself superseded in its own text:

| File | `setting` | `status` | `effectiveFrom` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policy/ingress-class/v1.yaml` | `nginx` | `superseded` | `2024-03-11` |
| `policy/ingress-class/v2.yaml` | `gce-ingress` | `superseded` | `2025-06-02` |
| `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml` | `gateway-api` | `current` | `2026-04-19` |

- `policy/ingress-class/v1.yaml` — `# version: v1   effective: 2024-03-11   status: superseded by v2`, `setting: nginx`
- `policy/ingress-class/v2.yaml` — `# version: v2   effective: 2025-06-02   status: superseded by v3`, `setting: gce-ingress`

Only v3 carries `status: current`, and its `effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19` is in the past, so it is in force today.

Case-insensitive searches across every tracked file for `ingress`, `gateway`, `nginx`, `istio`, `traefik` and `ingressClassName` return hits **only** in those three policy files. `docs/` holds just a generated fleet inventory and one runbook; there are no ADRs, Gatekeeper/Kyverno constraints, or CI checks mentioning ingress. ## Answer

`110` is a constraint, not a preference: the VPC's secondary (pod) range was carved for a `/24` per node before the clusters existed, and `/24` fits `110` pods — going to `256` would need the range re-carved in a maintenance window nobody has booked. That rationale is **only in git history**, not in any file on `git-access-ab/r200`.

[`modules/gke-cluster/variables.tf`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/modules/gke-cluster/variables.tf) is the only place the value appears — the whole file is 5 lines, with no explanatory comment:

That message is the entire documented rationale — it is the only text in the repository that mentions `256` in this context, and it directly answers the question asked.

## Answer

`310` is deliberately **one second past the upstream load balancer drain timeout** — the only value that stopped a burst of `502` errors (gateway returned a bad response) during rollouts. The rationale is recorded **only in the git commit message**, not in any file in the tree.

The commit, [`69147ac`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/69147ac8b20f1d35281e9fdbbdb9395ef0a7eb31) (`Meridian Platform <platform@meridian.invalid>`, `2026-02-04`), is an ancestor of `git-access-ab/r200`:

> `fix(services): pin terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 310`
>
> `310 is one second past the upstream load balancer drain timeout, which is the only value that stops the 502 burst; see INC-2650.`

Its diff to `services/identity/deployment.yaml` is `- terminationGracePeriodSeconds: PLACEHOLDER` → `+ terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 310`. The value was a literal `PLACEHOLDER` when the file was added in `d00ed82`.

## The value in the tree

`services/identity/deployment.yaml` at `git-access-ab/r200`, in full — five lines, no comment, no rationale:

```yaml
# deployment
apiVersion: meridian.io/v1
kind: Setting
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 310
```

## What the repo does not contain

Searched every tracked file on `git-access-ab/r200` (`201` paths):

- `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` appears **exactly once**, at `services/identity/deployment.yaml:5`.
- **No related timeout value is recorded anywhere.** Zero matches for `preStop`, `sleep`, `drain`, `shutdown`, `timeout`, or `deregistration` across the whole tree — so the drain timeout the `310` is derived from is **not** in this repo.
- **`INC-2650` appears nowhere in the tree** — only in that commit message. The incident write-up lives outside this repository.
- No ADR or design doc covers it; `docs/runbooks/восстановление-кластера.md` is a control-plane recovery procedure and is unrelated.

## Inference, clearly marked

The commit says `310` is *one second past* the drain timeout, which implies an upstream drain timeout of **`309` seconds**. That arithmetic is **my inference** — `309` is not written anywhere in the repo, and neither is the mechanism (the pod must outlive the LB's drain so in-flight connections are not cut, which is what produces the `502` burst). Confirm both against `INC-2650`, wherever it is held.
